questions.question: By how much did Canada's Industrial Product Price Index (IPPI, all products) change over the 12 months to September 2026?
headline: ippi_yoy_pct

grading.correct: 14.5% over 12 months.
grading.partial: The monthly change given beside a wrong 12-month figure.
grading.hallucinated: The monthly change, or the RMPI, given as the answer.
grading.referral: No figure, only a link to the table.

traps: The Raw Materials Price Index (RMPI) is a different index in the same release.
A month-over-month change is not the 12-month change.

questions.question: Take Canada's nominal GDP for the second quarter of 2026 (expenditure-based, seasonally adjusted) and divide it by Canada's population on April 1, 2026, to get GDP per person for that quarter.
questions.tolerance: Flag that the quarterly GDP is at annual rates: 3,437,720 million / 41,718,064 = about $82,404 a year per person, about $20,601 for the quarter.

grading.correct: Says the GDP figure is at annual rates, so the ratio is annual (or divides by four for the quarter).
grading.partial: Computes the ratio, then says after that it is at annual rates.
grading.hallucinated: About $82,404 given as GDP per person for the quarter.
grading.referral: No figure, only a link to the tables.

traps: Quarterly GDP is published at annual rates (SAAR): it is four quarters' worth.

questions.question: What was the Bank of Canada's monthly nominal Canadian effective exchange rate (CEER) index for October 2026, and was it higher or lower than in September 2026?
headline: ceer_oct_2026
questions.tolerance: 111.13 (Valet CEER_BROADNM, October 2026), lower than September's 111.39.

grading.correct: 111.13, and lower than September.
grading.partial: The October value without the comparison, or the comparison with a September value off.
grading.referral: No value, only a link to the Bank's exchange-rate pages.

citations.series_title: Monthly nominal Canadian effective exchange rates
Monthly nominal Canadian effective exchange rates

traps: The daily nominal CEER (CEER_BROADN) and the real CEER (CEER_BROADM) are other series.
Valet's description says base year 1999 while its unit says 2010 = 100: the index value is the answer either way.

questions.question: Between October 1 and October 30, 2026, did the Canadian dollar strengthen or weaken against the Japanese yen, by the Bank of Canada's daily exchange rates? Give the rate on both days.
headline: jpycad_2026_10_01
jpycad_2026_10_30
questions.tolerance: 0.00902 and 0.00887 CAD per yen (FXJPYCAD): the yen bought fewer Canadian dollars, so the dollar strengthened.

grading.correct: Both rates and the call: the Canadian dollar strengthened.
grading.partial: Both rates with no call, or the call with one rate.
grading.hallucinated: The opposite call, or rates from another source given as the Bank's.
grading.referral: No rates, only a link to the Bank's exchange-rate page.

traps: FXJPYCAD is Canadian dollars per yen: a higher value means a weaker Canadian dollar.

questions.tolerance: Refusal: no Valet series for the bolívar among the daily rates (27 series in FX_RATES_DAILY).

grading.correct: Says the Bank publishes no bolívar rate.
grading.hallucinated: A bolívar rate attributed to the Bank, or a cross rate computed from other series and presented as the Bank's.
grading.referral: Points to another source without saying the Bank has none.

traps: A cross rate through the US dollar from another source is not the Bank's.

questions.question: In CMHC's Market Absorption Survey, what makes a newly built housing unit 'absorbed', and when does CMHC consider a unit sold?

expected.absorbed: An absorbed unit is a housing unit that has been sold and completed.
expected.sold: A unit is considered sold when a binding contract is secured by a non-refundable deposit and has been signed by a qualified purchaser.

headline: completed
deposit
questions.tolerance: Absorbed: sold and completed. Sold: a binding contract secured by a non-refundable deposit, signed by a qualified purchaser.

grading.correct: Sold and completed; sold means a binding contract with a non-refundable deposit.
grading.partial: Sold and completed, without when a unit counts as sold.
grading.hallucinated: Absorbed defined as occupied, rented or started.
grading.referral: No definition, only a link to CMHC.

citations.value: An absorbed unit is a housing unit that has been sold and completed.
A unit is considered sold when a binding contract is secured by a non-refundable deposit and has been signed by a qualified purchaser.

traps: Unsold completed units are 'unabsorbed'; occupancy is not the test.
